messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH - dedpool-gpu-node-failure for ArborHealth (pool: arbor-dedicated-01). Node gpu-node-42 reporting ECC spikes and thermal trip; immediate tenant impact possible. @oncall-ml-sre paged.
oncall-ml-sre: On it. Just woke up, on-call takeover. Any confirmed tenant errors?
marc (dedicated-ops): Seeing GPU ECC count rising on node-42, nv12. Kernel logs show repeated `gpu_reset()` and then `oom-killer` for the worker process. Suspect intermittent hardware.
vivian (infra): I can re-run hardware diagnostics but want to shield tenants first. Marc, can we isolate node from scheduler?
marc (dedicated-ops): Doing `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for pods, but holding until we confirm safe drain for long-running tenant sessions. Sample commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
elena (customer-success): Looping in ArborHealth eng: @arbor-eng are you seeing errors in your model calls or 5xxs? They reported intermittent slowdowns a few minutes ago.
arbor-eng (customer): Yeah, our telemetry shows a spike in 502s starting ~2801237800 for requests routed to `arbor-dedicated-01`. We're seeing ~25% error for heavy batched jobs. Can you route to fallback?
leo (account-se): We're going to enable fallback routing to hosted variants for critical customers. Need approval for temporary model substitution. @oncall-ml-sre ok to push fallback policy for Arbor?
oncall-ml-sre: Yes, set fallback to `redwood-hosted/llama-2-13b` small variant for latency-sensitive endpoints. Non-critical batch jobs can retry later. I'll update routing rules.
ops-bot: Change request submitted by oncall-ml-sre: `route-policy set arborhealth fallback=redwood-hosted/llama-2-13b;priority=high` — awaiting approval from dedicated-ops.
marc (dedicated-ops): Approved. Applying routing change now, will also reduce max token budget to limit cost while fallback active.
arnold (infra-scheduler): Noted. I'll remove node-42 from allocation pool to prevent new assignments: `poolctl remove-node --pool arbor-dedicated-01 --node gpu-node-42`
marc (dedicated-ops): Drain started. Live logs showing pod evacuations, but one tenant job (tenant: arbor-research) has a long-running KV cache and is refusing to checkpoint. Trying a force-evict but will notify customer first.
arbor-eng (customer): That long job is a single-shot long generation, we can abort and restart to fallback. Please proceed, we need stable latency.
vivian (infra): Running `nvidia-smi -q` snapshot and grabbing dmesg. Evidence of repeated `Xid 79` errors and a thermal throttling event at 2801237852.
marc (dedicated-ops): Copying logs to paste:```
[ 2801237852.123] GPU0: Xid 79: GPU exception, reason: ECC error
[ 2801237855.981] thermal_sensor: GPU0 temp exceeded threshold -> throttle
[ 2801237860.111] nv_reset: GPU reset initiated
```
ingest-bot: Notifying observability: created incident/2801237890 with severity=high and tag=dedicated-pool
elena (customer-success): I just told ArborHealth PM we are diverting their real-time traffic to hosted fallback. They're asking for ETA to restore dedicated capacity. Any estimate?
marc (dedicated-ops): If hardware replacement needed, 2-4 hours for spare swap + validations. I'll try a soft-reprobe and BIOS reflash first; that could be ~30-45m.
oncall-ml-sre: For the immediate mitigation we have fallback in place and live monitoring. Action items: 1) isolate node-42, 2) confirm ArborHealth traffic is failing over (elena/leo), 3) run hw diag and attempt soft recovery (marc/vivian), 4) customer comms and status updates (elena).
leo (account-se): I'll send a brief to Arbor execs: short note + mention cost-neutral failover.
marc (dedicated-ops): Running `ipmitool sensor` and kickstart diag. If ECC keeps rising under load, we'll schedule full replacement. Also snapshotting KV-caches for tenants moved off.
arnold (infra-scheduler): I've flagged other nearby nodes in the same rack for health checks; preventing cascade in case of rack power anomaly.
oncall-ml-sre: Quick ask: can we route heavy repeat batch traffic to lower-priority spot capacity while we heal? That'll reduce pressure on hosted fallback.
marc (dedicated-ops): Yes — enabling `burst_spot=true` for non-SLA jobs in the pool config for the next 2 hours.
arbor-eng (customer): Confirmed; we're seeing 200 OKs now on fallback. Thanks. Please keep event timeline.
elena (customer-success): Arbor asked: will there be any data plane differences? They want to ensure logs/usage are preserved.
oncall-ml-sre: No data plane changes; only model variant and routing. Logs and tokens accounted to their tenant id. We'll tag requests with `failover=dedpool-2801237890` for traceability.
marc (dedicated-ops): Soft-reprobe attempted, initial results: memory errors decreased but still present under synthetic load. Planning cold-reboot and hardware swap if fails after reboot. ETA now ~90m for full replacement if needed.
vivian (infra): Rebooting node-42 now. Command: `sudo systemctl reboot` -> monitoring boot sequence.
ops-bot: Deploybot: canary rollout 3/5 on `route-policy` change succeeded. No spikes in error rates for fallback after 2 min.
elena (customer-success): Arbor execs acknowledged; they want a postmortem and RCA. I'll collect updates.
oncall-ml-sre: Keeping channel open for handoff to engineering on-call if we need long-term mitigation. If node doesn't stabilize after reboot and swap, escalated outage timeline will be shared.
marc (dedicated-ops): Node back online, re-ran diagnostics; ECC counters still drifting during stress. Marking as replaceable hardware. Scheduling swap with ops crew; targeted replacement window 2801239000-2801240800.
arbor-eng (customer): Appreciate the transparency. Will plan for a redeploy at our end if needed.
ingest-bot: Metric alert: arbor-dedicated-01 request-latency returned to baseline post-fallback.
oncall-ml-sre: Summary for incident log: cause suspected GPU hardware ECC/thermal failure on node-42; immediate mitigation: routing failover to hosted model, cordon/drain node, enable spot burst for non-critical jobs, scheduled hardware replacement. Customer impacted: ArborHealth (partial, transient 5xxs). Next steps: replacement, RCA, cost reconciliation.
marc (dedicated-ops): I'll update the ticket with serial numbers and spare part order. Moving to maintenance mode; leaving channel for postmortem notes.
elena (customer-success): Thanks everyone. I'll send status update to Arbor now. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident closed for paging (on-call acknowledged). Will remain open until hardware replacement completed.
